# Metascape Gene List Function
This writes a text file that can be read in metascape to generate gene list analyses.

```{r}
# Function

# gene_lists: a named list, e.g. list(RNA_mediated_noIR = c("DKC1","NHP2",...), ...)
# writes the "#Name / Genes" tab-separated format (comma-joined gene column),
# with CRLF line endings, matching multiple_list_symbol.txt
write_multi_gene_list <- function(gene_lists, file) {
  header <- c(
    "#Name\tGenes",
    "# (1) All lines start with # are ignored;",
    "# (2) Two columns: Name and Genes must be tab-seprated;",
    "# (3) Gene identifiers are contatenated within the second column by space/comma/semicolon, space/comma/semicolon must not be part of the gene identifier."
  )
  body <- imap_chr(gene_lists, ~ paste0(.y, "\t", paste(.x, collapse = ",")))

  con <- file(file, open = "wb")   # binary connection so sep is written exactly as given, no platform translation
  writeLines(c(header, body), con, sep = "\r\n")
  close(con)
}

# Usage (template: replace the <PLACEHOLDERS>)
# each has to be a named vector list that can be passed to the write_multi_gene_list function
# minimum is 2 lists; add more entries in the same format as needed
gene_lists <- list(
  # <listname_1> = <vector_1>,
  # <listname_2> = <vector_2>
)

write_multi_gene_list(gene_lists, "<output_dir>/<output_name>.txt")

```

```{r}
# Function to clean up featureCounts matrix with both gene id and gene name column
process_feature_counts <- function(file_path) {
  # Read matrix, skipping the first comment line
  fc <- read.table(file_path, sep="\t", header=TRUE, comment.char="#", 
                   check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  
  # Identify sample columns (BAM files typically start at column 8 in this setup)
  col_names <- colnames(fc)
  bam_cols <- 8:length(col_names)
  
  # Clean sample column names: split by '/', take last; split by '.', take first 2
  cleaned_names <- sapply(col_names[bam_cols], function(x) {
    base_name <- tail(strsplit(x, "/")[[1]], 1)
    parts <- strsplit(base_name, "\\.")[[1]]
    paste(parts[1:min(2, length(parts))], collapse=".")
  })
  colnames(fc)[bam_cols] <- cleaned_names
  
  # Identify columns where all values are 0
  is_zero <- sapply(fc[, bam_cols, drop=FALSE], function(x) all(x == 0))
  cols_to_drop <- names(is_zero)[is_zero]
  
  # Drop zero-columns and print them
  if (length(cols_to_drop) > 0) {
    cat("Samples Dropped (due to no reads):", paste(cols_to_drop, collapse=", "), "\n")
    fc <- fc[, !(colnames(fc) %in% cols_to_drop)]
  } else {
    cat("Samples Dropped (due to no reads): None\n")
  }
  
  # Drop the spatial coordinates (keeping Geneid and gene_name)
  cols_to_remove <- c("Chr", "Start", "End", "Strand", "Length")
  fc <- fc[, !(colnames(fc) %in% cols_to_remove)]
  
  return(fc)
}

# --- Subtraction Logic ---

# 1. Process both files
exon_df <- process_feature_counts("featureCounts_trimmed.exon.counts.txt")
gene_df <- process_feature_counts("featureCounts_trimmed.gene.counts.txt")

# 2. Sort both dataframes by Geneid to ensure rows align perfectly
exon_df <- exon_df[order(exon_df$Geneid), ]
gene_df <- gene_df[order(gene_df$Geneid), ]

# 3. Create the final intronic dataframe retaining ID columns
intron_df <- gene_df[, c("Geneid", "gene_name")]

# 4. Identify the intersecting sample columns
samples <- intersect(colnames(gene_df)[-(1:2)], colnames(exon_df)[-(1:2)])

# 5. Subtract exon counts from gene counts
intron_df[samples] <- gene_df[samples] - exon_df[samples]

# 6. Floor any negative values to 0 (caused by rare read summarization overlaps)
intron_df[samples][intron_df[samples] < 0] <- 0

```
